config.title: Build multi tenant context resolver middleware

intro.title: Build multi tenant context resolver middleware
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a middleware function for a Node.js application that resolves and attaches a tenant context to incoming HTTP requests, enabling multi-tenant support. You will learn the core concept of middleware by creating a function that processes requests before they reach your main route handlers. The main technologies involved are the Express.js framework and JavaScript functions for handling HTTP request and response objects. By the end, you will understand how to extract tenant information from requests and make it available throughout your application in a clean, reusable way.
intro.usecase: Multi-tenant context resolver middleware is essential in SaaS platforms where a single application serves multiple customers (tenants) with isolated data and configurations. For example, in a dashboard application like Salesforce or HubSpot, this middleware ensures each company sees only their own customer data, reports, and custom settings when users log in. Developers implement this pattern to securely route requests, apply tenant-specific configurations, and maintain data isolation without duplicating code. This approach allows platforms to scale efficiently while providing personalized experiences for each tenant.

objectives: Construct a middleware function that extracts tenant identifiers from incoming HTTP requests
Initialize a tenant context object with resolved tenant configuration and data
Integrate the tenant resolver middleware into an Express.js application pipeline
Manipulate request objects to attach tenant context for downstream handlers
Configure the middleware to handle missing or invalid tenant identifiers gracefully
Apply the tenant context in route handlers to demonstrate multi-tenant data isolation
Control middleware execution order to ensure tenant resolution occurs before business logic

steps.instruction: Import the 'http' module for server creation and the 'url' module for parsing request URLs.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import Node.js built-in modules. You'll need both modules for this middleware lesson.
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have both 'http' and 'url' modules imported using require().
successCriteria: Both 'http' and 'url' modules are imported using require().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.instruction: Create a function called 'tenantResolver' that takes three parameters: request, response, and next callback.
steps.hint: Define a function with the name tenantResolver that accepts (req, res, next) as parameters.

steps.title: Extract the hostname from the incoming request
steps.instruction: Inside the tenantResolver middleware function, extract the 'host' header from the request object and store it in a variable called hostname.
steps.hint: In Node.js middleware, request headers are accessible via req.headers. Use req.headers.host to get the host header value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The middleware function will have a hostname variable containing the value from the request's host header.
successCriteria: The tenantResolver function contains a hostname variable assigned from req.headers.host.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're extracting the 'host' header specifically and storing it in a variable called hostname.
steps.feedbackWrong: The host header extraction is missing or incorrect. Remember to access req.headers.host and assign it to a hostname variable.

steps.title: Parse the hostname to extract the tenant identifier
steps.instruction: Inside the tenantResolver function, split the extracted hostname by dots and assign the first segment to a variable called tenantId.
steps.hint: Use the split() method on the hostname string with '.' as the separator, then access the first element of the resulting array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The tenantResolver function will now have a tenantId variable containing the first part of the hostname (e.g., 'acme' from 'acme.example.com').
successCriteria: The hostname is split using split('.') and the first segment is assigned to a variable named tenantId.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're splitting the hostname string and storing the first segment in a variable called tenantId.
steps.feedbackWrong: split the hostname by dots and extract the first segment as the tenant identifier.

steps.title: Validate the tenant identifier
steps.instruction: Inside the tenantResolver function, after extracting the tenant identifier, add validation to check if it exists and is not empty. If it's missing or empty, set it to a default value like 'default'.
steps.hint: You can use an if statement to check if the tenant identifier is truthy (exists and not empty). If not, assign a default string value to it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The tenant identifier will be validated and assigned a default value if missing, ensuring the middleware can proceed without errors.
successCriteria: The tenantResolver function includes validation that checks if tenantId exists and is not empty, and sets it to 'default' when invalid.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to check both existence and non-emptiness of tenantId. Use an if statement with a logical NOT operator to handle both cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation logic appears to be missing or incorrect. Remember to check if tenantId is falsy (undefined, null, or empty string) and assign 'default' in that case.

steps.title: Attach tenant context to the request object
steps.instruction: Inside the tenantResolver function, add the tenantId to the request object as a property named 'tenant'.
steps.hint: You can attach custom properties to the request object by assigning them directly, like req.propertyName = value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The request object will have a 'tenant' property containing the tenant identifier, making it accessible to subsequent middleware or route handlers.
successCriteria: The request object has a 'tenant' property set to the tenantId value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're adding the tenantId to the request object as a property named 'tenant'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The tenant context wasn't properly attached. Remember to assign the tenantId to req.tenant.

steps.instruction: Create a basic HTTP server using the http.createServer method to test the middleware.
steps.hint: Use the http module's createServer method to create a server instance. You can pass your middleware as an argument to createServer.

steps.title: Implement the server request handler with middleware
steps.instruction: Create a request handler function that calls the tenantResolver middleware before processing the request. Name this function 'requestHandler'.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes request and response parameters, calls tenantResolver with those parameters and a next callback, then sends a response with the tenant context.
steps.expectedOutcome: A requestHandler function is defined that integrates the tenantResolver middleware and sends a response containing the tenant context.
successCriteria: The requestHandler function is defined, calls tenantResolver with req, res, and a next callback, and sends a response that includes the tenantId.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a request handler, but make sure it calls tenantResolver with the correct parameters (req, res, next) and sends a response with the tenantId.
steps.feedbackWrong: The request handler is missing or doesn't properly integrate the middleware. Ensure you define a function that calls tenantResolver and sends a response.

steps.title: Add response logic that uses the tenant context
steps.instruction: In the request handler function, send a response that includes the tenant identifier from the request object's tenant context.
steps.hint: Access the tenant identifier from req.tenant and include it in the response body using res.end().
steps.expectedOutcome: The request handler will respond with a message containing the tenant identifier, demonstrating how downstream handlers can access the tenant context.
successCriteria: The request handler sends a response that includes the tenant identifier from req.tenant.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're accessing req.tenant and including it in the response body with res.end().
steps.feedbackWrong: The response logic doesn't yet use the tenant context. Check that you're accessing req.tenant and including it in the response.
